paragraphs: Apple has set some rules meant to curb unwanted iPhone notification ads, but some apps appear to be ignoring them.
iPhone users have reported promos with no opt-out and ads in Live Activities. Apple’s guidelines address both, but people say the practices continue.

Apple’s App Store Review Guidelines allow apps to send promotional push notifications. But there’s a catch. Users have to explicitly opt in through consent language in the app, with developers providing a way to opt out.
Live Activities face stricter limits: Apple tells developers “Don’t use a Live Activity to display ads or promotions” and also bars using Live Activities to send unsolicited messages.
In a post on X, Joe Rossignol wrote that several apps on his iPhone in Canada sent him prompts with no way to opt out. He named Cineplex, McDonald’s and Wendy’s.
And while Skip, a food-delivery app, offered a promo toggle, it kept sending promos even after switching the option off.
AliExpress is also reportedly showing ads in Live Activities, which conflicts with Apple’s design guidance.

To be fair, Apple broke the rules itself a few times. It reportedly sent an App Store notification promoting a Paramount+ subscription deal. Apple’s other apps have also drawn similar complaints before. One example is a Wallet notification promoting an F1 offer.
